25.0.0.en: "The kingdom of heaven": that is, God's heavenly reign over the hearts of His children in the Church, in preparation for the eternal Kingdom.

25.0.1.en: "Ten": a number that signifies completeness, that is, all mankind who believe in God.

25.0.2.en: "Virgins": they signify the human souls that believe in God.

25.0.3.en: "Their lamps": they signify the abilities of man, that is, spirit and body, by which he lives with God, so that his life is illumined.

25.0.5.en: So all are believers and their goal is eternity, that is, being with the Bridegroom forever. But they differ in how they prepare for the Kingdom.

25.1.0.en: "Five": this indicates the five senses of man, which he uses either well, like the wise virgins, or hands over to evil, like the foolish.

25.1.1.en: "Wise": they had the appearance of piety and its depth, which is the oil in the lamps.

25.1.2.en: "Foolish": these are the ones who had the appearance of the spiritual life, but had no oil, which is the love of God and the service of others.

25.1.3.en: And foolishness is that a person has the ability to enjoy God and fellowship with Him in this life and forever, and is negligent in this out of laziness and preoccupation with the world and its many concerns.

25.2.0.en: "Slumbered ... and slept": that is, the end of life and death.

25.2.1.en: The life of these virgins ended and they died, because the Bridegroom, that is, Christ, had not yet come.

25.3.0.en: "At midnight": this indicates the second coming of Christ after the repose of souls, and the revealing of His just judgment, where He rewards those who fell asleep in the faith, and recompenses those whom the darkness of the wicked world swallowed up. "A cry": the voices of the angels with the last trumpet calling the believers to salvation, and the wicked to judgment. "Go ye out to meet him": the bodies of the departed are changed, and gathered after their decomposition, and become spiritual bodies united with their spirits, to meet Christ and stand before Him on the Day of Judgment.

25.3.1.en: At the second coming of Christ, the bodies rise, and all mankind gathers on the Day of Judgment.

25.4.0.en: All the virgins came forward, that is, all mankind, to stand before God the just Judge. And each one gathered what he had of faith and love, that is, trimmed his lamp, and stood to be judged before God.

25.4.1.en: And only here the foolish realized that faith without love, that is, the oil, is of no benefit and the lamp goes out, because faith without works is dead; the demons believe and tremble, but they will not be saved. The foolish virgins tried to take oil from the wise, but they excused themselves because it would not suffice for them and for the foolish, and they should look for this oil and buy it from the sellers, that is, offer love and mercy to others, because good works, however much a person does, do not exceed and overflow beyond him so that he can give them to others. And Christ's saying is clear: "So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do" (Lk 17:10).

25.4.2.en: "Them that sell": that is, every person with whom we can do a work of mercy, such as the poor and needy.

25.5.0.en: The foolish virgins tried to show mercy and do good on the Day of Judgment, but there was no longer any opportunity. For Christ took the wise virgins and went in with them to the Kingdom, and the door was shut, and there was no longer any opportunity for anyone to enter after that.

25.5.2.en: "The door was shut": this means the guarantee of the wise virgins' permanence in the Kingdom, and the preventing of the wicked and Satan from entering, so that the righteous face no troubles in the Kingdom.

25.5.3.en: And on the other hand, there is no opportunity at all for the wicked to escape eternal torment far from God.

25.6.0.en: "Afterward": that is, after it was too late and they were sentenced to judgment.

25.6.1.en: "Open to us": they ask for a place in the Kingdom.

25.6.2.en: "I know you not": He does not know them as disciples and followers of His.

25.6.3.en: The foolish virgins tried to enter after the door was shut, but Christ refused, and even declared that He did not know them, that is, He has no relationship with them, because they had the appearance of piety and not its power and depth, that is, faith without works of love.

25.6.4.en: Whoever does not live in the love of God on earth has no place to enjoy His love in heaven.

25.7.0.en: Christ comments plainly, affirming the importance of spiritual watchfulness, that is, constant preparation for His coming, because we do not know its time.

25.7.1.en: God awaits your practical love in care for your holy worship of Him, and good works with everyone you meet. So seize the opportunity of your life to do good as far as you are able, and your life on earth will be illumined, and you will not be put to shame on the Day of Judgment.

25.8.0.en: "Travelling": by Christ's ascension to heaven, He left mankind for the length of their lives, to strive in their spiritual life on earth until His second coming.

25.8.1.en: "His goods": all the abilities of mankind are divine gifts with which they are entrusted as stewards for God, and they will give an account for them on the last day.

25.8.2.en: "According to his several ability": all the abilities that he can use, for God did not withhold His gifts from anyone, and did not give him abilities greater than his capacity, lest he be confused by them or show his inability.

25.8.3.en: "Took his journey": He left mankind in their freedom to invest their abilities throughout their lives.

25.8.4.en: God likened Himself to a man and mankind to His servants, and gave them talents, that is, money, to trade with and invest, and travelled for an unknown time.

25.8.5.en: And God's gifts and endowments differ from one person to another, for some receive more than others, and God will judge each one according to what he received, so let not him who received more be proud, and let not him who received less envy or be jealous; what matters is faithfulness in investing the abilities of mankind that God has given them, many or few.

25.9.0.en: The one who had five talents traded, signifying one who invested his five senses, and gained five other talents, that is, he came to have the inner senses, which are the ability to know God, and not only knowledge of the material world around him, that is, he came to have the inner eye, which is insight, and the inner ear, that is, hearing the voice of God... and so on.

25.9.1.en: As for the one who had two talents, and the number two signifies love, like the bridegroom and his bride, when he traded with his two talents, he also gained two other talents, that is, his love was doubled, so it became for God and also for all mankind.

25.10.0.en: The last servant, who had one talent, signifies the selfish person, that is, he loves himself only, for he is lazy and did not weary himself by offering love to God and to others, but hid his talent in the earth, that is, he was immersed in earthly desires and luxuriated in pleasures to satisfy his personal mood, forgetting that he is a steward over this talent, which is God's property.

25.10.1.en: Each of us is a steward over his life, because it is the property of God who bought us with His blood. So we must live for Him, faithful in investing all our abilities and gifts.

25.11.0.en: "After a long time": this is the long opportunity of life that God gave to every person, so that he may invest his abilities for the glory of His holy name.

25.11.1.en: After this life ends, the Day of Judgment comes, that is, the master comes to reckon with his servants.

25.12.0.en: The one who had five talents presented what he had gained, which was five other talents, and his master commended him and described him as good, because he lived for God and the love of others, and also faithful because he invested all his energies and achieved a profit of 100%. And he rewarded him for his faithfulness on earth, which is the little, by granting him life in the Kingdom where He gives him great blessings, which are expressed by the much, that is, he lives in love like a bride with her bridegroom forever in constant joy with God, his master and heavenly Father.

25.12.1.en: And it is understood from this that each one will be judged for himself, and for every divine gift given to him to invest, because he is a steward over it.

25.12.2.en: "Well": that is, rightly, and it is a praise from God than which there is none greater.

25.13.0.en: The second servant presented the two talents that he had gained like the first servant, and his master commended him like the first, in the same measure and with the same qualities, that he was good and faithful, and gave him the same reward, which is entering the Kingdom, because he achieved a complete profit, which is 100%.

25.14.0.en: The third servant was selfish and wicked, because he fell into negligence, and slipped into other sins, not only neglect and not using his abilities for God's account, that is, love of God and others, but, instead of loving others, he began to wrong them and also his master, that is, God, and described him as hard and greedy, taking though he had not given, and this is the opposite of the truth. But the sin that begins small with laziness and negligence leads to graver sins, and in the end causes the sinner to lose his spiritual insight.

25.14.1.en: His lying also appears when he says "I was afraid", though he did not fear God and strive spiritually, but was immersed in his earthly desires.

25.15.0.en: "Thou wicked and slothful servant": the master exposed the true reason for his not trading with the talent, which is his laziness and wickedness.

25.15.1.en: The master condemned this servant from the words of his mouth, for he said to him: if I am hard and greedy, it would have been better for you to trade with the talent, that is, to use it in material dealings to acquire a profit, and by that He means investing his abilities in the love of God and others.

25.15.2.en: "The exchangers": where money is used in trade to make a profit, and what is meant is offering love to others. And the exchangers are the specialists in financial dealings, so they signify the fathers and spiritual guides, for when one who walks spiritually obeys them, they guide him how to invest his abilities for the glory of God.

25.15.3.en: "Usury": the gain that comes from trade, and its meaning here is winning souls for Christ by doing good.

25.16.0.en: God's punishment of him was first to strip him of his abilities, and then to give them to the one who had come to have ten talents, affirming that everyone who has faithfulness and the love of God is given by God increasing gifts. But as for him who has no love of God and others and is unfaithful, God takes away his gifts from him because he does not deserve them.

25.17.0.en: The idle (wicked) servant is punished by being cast into eternal torment, expressed by the outer darkness far from God, where there is intense sorrow and violent pain signified by weeping and gnashing of teeth. Be faithful in using your abilities and God's blessings on you will increase, and do not neglect any grace or time available to you (a talent), lest God deprive you of your eternal inheritance.

25.18.s.en: (3) The coming of Christ and the work of mercy

25.18.0.en: After Christ spoke of His second coming in a symbolic way as a bridegroom of the soul or as a master of his servants, He speaks here plainly about the Day of Judgment on which He comes as Judge in great glory, different from the image of weakness in which He lived in the body on earth from His birth in the manger until He was crucified on the Cross. He will come with His angels and sit on the throne of His glory, that is, His throne, to judge the whole world for their deeds in every place and time, and He separates mankind by means of His angels into the righteous, whom He sets on His right hand, for the right hand signifies blessing and strength, while the wicked He sets on His left, a sign of shame and disgrace.

25.18.1.en: And the distinction will be very easy for God, as the shepherd distinguishes the flock he tends, whether sheep or goats. And the sheep are more obedient and peaceable and submissive to the shepherd than the goats.

25.18.2.en: And it is clear from Christ's words that in the end there are only two groups, the righteous and the wicked, and He calls them the wise and the foolish, or the faithful servants and the unfaithful, and here He calls them the sheep and the goats. And there is no third place, as some claim, for torturing and punishing the wicked temporarily and then joining them to the righteous.

25.19.0.en: Christ the King describes the believers as blessed, and as children of God, His Father and their Father, that is, He declares His fellowship with them in love, and that He is the firstborn among many brethren, so He calls them "blessed of my Father", and welcomes them to inherit His Kingdom, which He prepared for them before they were created, to enjoy with Him in it forever.

25.20.0.en: Christ enumerates the works of mercy that the righteous performed, and for which they deserved the inheritance of the Kingdom of Heaven, ascribing the work of mercy to Himself, so He mentions their feeding the hungry and thirsty, materially or spiritually, and their care for strangers, so that they host them, and this care not only meets their needs, but reassures them psychologically to continue life in the new place.

25.20.1.en: If you meet a stranger anywhere, welcome him and make him feel at home, and open the way for all so that they may be satisfied with Christ, our true food.

25.21.0.en: He also mentions clothing the naked, whether with garments or with the righteousness of Christ by walking in virtue. And in sickness, a person feels his weakness, and is moved by the love of those who ask after him, and it is a suitable opportunity to speak to him about God.

25.21.1.en: And among the hardest cases also are those imprisoned, who have lost their freedom and the ability to go to their loved ones, so when their loved ones come to them they rejoice greatly, and we offer them Christ who never leaves them, even if they are far from people in prison.

25.22.0.en: Christ makes clear how the work of mercy is directed to Him personally, so He sets up a gentle dialogue between the righteous and Himself, and they ask Him humbly: when saw we thee, Lord, an hungered or thirsty or sick... and so on, because they feel that they are not worthy of this praise. And He answers them that all that they did of works of mercy with the weak, the poor, the sick or the imprisoned was offered to Him personally. And this is a great divine appreciation of the work of mercy, and indeed a declaration that it is the summit of love and our way to inheriting the Kingdom.

25.22.1.en: "The least": that is, the needy and the weak.

25.23.0.en: Christ calls the wicked on His left, and describes them as deserving the divine curse and eternal torment, though they should have been in the Kingdom that He prepared for them, but they refused to respond to His love. So He casts them now far from Him, and deprives them of His love, which they refused, and they will be forever in the torment of the fire prepared for the devil and his fallen angels, who are the demons, that is, they now become like the demons because they refused the love of God.

25.24.0.en: Christ declares the reason for their going to eternal torment, which is their selfishness, and their refusing to feel for others and help them in their various needs.

25.25.0.en: The wicked ask when they saw God in need and did not give to Him, so He declares to them that He was in the form of the needy and of those small in their standing and abilities, and they refused to show mercy to them.

25.26.0.en: Christ affirms that the Day of Judgment is the end, for the righteous continue in the enjoyment of the eternal Kingdom, while the wicked are tormented forever also.

25.26.1.en: This is your opportunity now for repentance and feeling for others and doing mercy with all who are around you and all whom you meet, before the dreadful Day of Judgment comes.

25.26.2.en: The Passover; the Lord's Supper; the arrest of Christ and His trial
